claims.text: Pre-straining NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 induces local short-range order.
The induced short-range order increases the population of hard atomic motifs.
Hard atomic motifs strengthen local stress fields and enhance dislocation pinning.
Mechanically induced short-range order raises the yield strength of NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 during high-temperature tensile testing.
Mechanically induced short-range order modulates the ductility of NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 during high-temperature tensile testing.
The as-processed NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 alloy has a random or near-random atomic distribution and a baseline dislocation density.
The nanoscale SRO motifs and their associated local stress fields act as barriers to slip.
Moderate pre-strain promotes atomic reordering into clusters that obstruct dislocation motion.
SRO-induced dislocation pinning enhances yield strength and alters failure modes.
Too little or too much pre-strain fails to optimize short-range order.
Insufficient or excessive pre-strain produces mechanical behavior closer to the as-processed or over-deformed baselines than does moderate pre-strain.
An intermediate pre-strain level will produce higher yield strength than both the as-processed and excessively pre-strained states.
An intermediate pre-strain level will produce more homogeneous plastic deformation and reduced strain localization relative to both comparison states.
Quantified short-range-order levels will systematically correlate with shifts in mechanical properties.
The proposed mechanism is expected to operate in NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 from room temperature to approximately 873 K.
Deformation-induced increases in dislocation density or possible precipitation may contribute to the measured mechanical changes independently of short-range order.
